newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma to debate Yeltsin removal Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma to debate Yeltsin removal Wednesday.

text.p: The State Duma lower house of the Russian parliament will on Wednesday debate a controversial draft document which would remove President Boris Yeltsin from office for health reasons, a Duma spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spokesman did not say why the Duma Council, which comprises heads of parliamentary factions, decided to debate the draft despite objections from parliament's legal department.
The legal experts have said a parliamentary declaration is not enough to dislodge the president or to start impeachment procedures.

The Russian constitution does not outline a mechanism under which a president can be ousted on health grounds and parliament's legal department has already ruled the draft invalid and unconstitutional.

The author of the draft document, communist Viktor Ilyukhin, told reporters on Tuesday he was determined to press ahead with the debate. "The ruling by the legal department has failed to change my point of view," he said.
The Kremlin has said a Duma decision would have no legal force on Yeltsin.

But officials have admitted a new attack on the president could prompt political confrontation between him and the largely conservative chamber. The presidential press office was not immediately available to comment on the decision.
Yeltsin, who turns 66 on February 1, spent most of the second half of 1996 away from the Kremlin due to heart problems which demanded multiple bypass surgery in November.

He returned to work briefly in December, but was taken to hospital with pneumonia on January 8 and stayed there until Monday, when he moved to a residence outside Moscow. On Tuesday the Kremlin said he was working on state papers and had no meetings scheduled.
The Kremlin insists that Yeltsin's pneumonia has nothing to do with his heart problems and that the president is in full control of the country.
Ilyukhin said he was not sure that the chamber, cautious not to trigger a major political confrontation with the president, would back his draft.
Another senior member of the powerful communist faction, Leonid Ivanchenko, has prepared another declaration calling Yeltsin to give up his duties voluntarily.
